statements.claim: The palm grove (talavana) let fall fruit in such abundance it kept falling and lay fallen, and no one had ever eaten any of it.
statements.evidence: BP 10.15.21 'phalāni tatra bhūrīṇi patanti patitāni ca' (fruit falling and fallen) and 10.15.24 'abhukta-pūrvāṇi phalāni' (fruit never before eaten).

statements.claim: The grove belonged to the demon Dhenuka, in donkey form, with his fierce kin; he had made men his food and people were afraid and kept their distance.
statements.evidence: BP 10.15.22-23 'khara-rūpa-dhṛk' (ass-form), 'kṛta-narāhārād bhītair nṛbhir' (men afraid of him who made men his food); kin mentioned in the episode's excerpt and 10.15.35.

statements.claim: The boys cried to Krishna and Balarama: 'Rama! Rama, mighty-armed! Krishna, destroyer of the wicked!' and begged 'Give us that fruit.'
statements.evidence: BP 10.15.20 'rāma rāma mahā-bāho kṛṣṇa duṣṭa-nibarhaṇa' and 10.15.25 'prayaccha tāni naḥ kṛṣṇa'.

statements.claim: The boys' minds were greedy with the fragrance, and Krishna, hearing his friends, wished only to please them.
statements.evidence: BP 10.15.25 'gandha-lobhita-cetasām' and 10.15.26 'suhṛd-vacaḥ śrutvā suhṛt-priya-cikīrṣayā'.

statements.claim: Krishna and Balarama set out for the palm grove with the boys following.
statements.evidence: Pack excerpt (10.15.20-26): the boys ask to be given the fruit; next event 10.15.27 has Balarama entering the grove (see DKS_0054 pack).

statements.claim: Atmosphere: afternoon warmth, the wind carrying the scent, the boys stopping their play.
statements.evidence: Generic scene-setting consistent with the forest setting of BP 10.15; no sourceable fact asserted.

notes: All factual claims map to BP 10.15.20-26; the 'grown men grazed elsewhere' detail is a fair inference from bhītair nṛbhir.

statements.claim: Balarama went to the palm trees and shook them so the ripe fruit came down in a shower.
statements.evidence: BP 10.15.27 'balaḥ praviśya bāhubhyāṃ tālān samparikampayan' (Balarama entered and shook the palms with his arms); VP 5.8: 'Sankarshańa and Krishńa shook the trees, and brought down the fruit.'

statements.claim: In that grove dwelt the fierce demon Dhenuka, who fed on the flesh of deer.
statements.evidence: VP 5.8: 'dwelt the fierce demon Dhenuka, feeding upon the flesh of deer' (BP 10.15.23 calls him kṛta-narāhāra, 'made men his food'; the story follows VP here, both in the pack).

statements.claim: Hearing the falling fruit, Dhenuka rushed in a great passion in his donkey form and kicked Balarama with his hind legs.
statements.evidence: BP 10.15.28-29: the asura-ass heard the sound of falling fruit, came speedily and struck Balarama with both feet; VP 5.8: 'began to kick Ráma on the breast with his hinder heels.'

statements.claim: Balarama caught him by the hind legs, whirled him with a single hand until he expired, and dashed him against a great palm tree.
statements.evidence: BP 10.15.31-32 'sa taṃ gṛhītvā prapador bhrāmayitvaika-pāṇinā' (seizing his hind feet, whirling with one hand) and 'tenāhato mahā-tālo' (struck against the great palm); VP 5.8 likewise.

statements.claim: The palm trembled from the blow and shook down fruit like rain poured by the wind; Dhenuka fell lifeless.
statements.evidence: BP 10.15.32 'vepamāno bṛhac-chirāḥ' (trembling, huge-headed); VP 5.8: 'struck down abundance of fruit, like rain drops poured upon earth by the wind.'

statements.claim: It was no wonder, the verses say, for the slayer is the infinite Lord of all the worlds.
statements.evidence: BP 10.15.34 'naitac citraṃ bhagavati hy anante jagad-īśvare' (this is not wonderful in the Blessed infinite Lord of the worlds).

statements.claim: Atmosphere: the brothers' easy rhythm, the boys' laughter, the grove growing quiet.
statements.evidence: Non-factual framing; no sourceable fact asserted.

notes: Tradition note re BP-vs-VP attribution (joint vs Rama alone) is correctly reflected; story keeps Balarama as shaker and slayer, consistent with both pack sources.

statements.claim: Dhenuka's kin, the other ass-demons, came rushing to avenge him and charged at Krishna and Balarama.
statements.evidence: BP 10.15.35-36 'jñātayo dhenukasya ye... āpatataḥ' (the kinsmen of Dhenuka came rushing).

statements.claim: Krishna and Balarama, as if at play, flung the charging donkeys lifeless among the palm trees, one after another.
statements.evidence: BP 10.15.36 'kṛṣṇo rāmaś ca līlayā' (as if in play); the grove strewn with lifeless demon bodies (10.15.37).

statements.claim: The gods and the wise heard of the great deed and rejoiced.
statements.evidence: BP 10.15.38 'tayos tat su-mahat karma niśamya vibudhādayaḥ' (the gods/wise hearing that great deed).

statements.claim: The people, their fear gone, came and ate the palm fruit, and the cattle grazed where they had never before dared.
statements.evidence: BP 10.15.39 'manuṣyā gata-sādhvasāḥ' (men without fear ate the palm fruit); beasts freely enjoying the grove appears in the pack's own index summary, and VP 5.8 (in the series) states the cattle grazed where they never before ventured.

statements.claim: Krishna stood with eyes like lotus petals, and his name and deeds were auspicious to hear.
statements.evidence: BP 10.15.40 'kṛṣṇaḥ kamala-patrākṣaḥ puṇya-śravaṇa-kīrtanaḥ' (lotus-eyed Krishna, whose name and praise are auspicious).

statements.claim: Atmosphere: hooves drumming, the grove quiet again, the terror gone.
statements.evidence: Scene-setting around the supported events.

statements.claim: At night a blazing forest fire rose from the dry woods and surrounded Vraja on every side.
statements.evidence: BP 10.17.20 'śuci-vanodbhūto dāvāgniḥ sarvato vrajam' (forest fire born of the dry forest, around all of Vraja); night setting in the pack's index title/summary.

statements.claim: The people woke, scorched and terrified, with no way out.
statements.evidence: BP 10.17.21 'sambhrāntā dahyamānā vrajaukasaḥ' (bewildered Vraja-dwellers, being burned).

statements.claim: They cried 'Krishna! Krishna! O greatly fortunate one! O Rama of boundless power!' and called the fire one no one can cross, like the fire that will end all things, begging Krishna to save his own people and friends.
statements.evidence: BP 10.17.22-23 'kṛṣṇa kṛṣṇa mahā-bhaga he rāmāmita-vikrama / su-dustarān naḥ svān pāhi kālāgneḥ suhṛdaḥ prabho' (O greatly fortunate Krishna, O Rama of boundless prowess, save your own friends from the all-destroying kālāgni).

statements.claim: The Lord of the world looked on his people's distress and drank up the whole fire.
statements.evidence: BP 10.17.24 'sva-jana-vaiklavyaṃ nirīkṣya jagad-īśvaraḥ' (the Lord of the world seeing his people's distress); pack excerpt: 'drinks the whole fire into himself.'

statements.claim: Atmosphere: the trusting sleep, smoke rising thick, the silence after the roar.
statements.evidence: Non-factual framing around the supported events.

statements.claim: While Krishna and Balarama tended the herd with the cowherds, a demon named Pralamba came in the shape of a cowherd to seize the boys and destroy the two brothers.
statements.evidence: BP 10.18.16 (Rama and Krishna tending cattle with the cowherds); pack excerpt: 'Pralamba, a demon in cowherd's form, enters the boys' games' intent on seizing the boys; Harivamsha 1.64 (series pack): came with a view to kill them.

statements.claim: The demon wore wild flowers and the easy manner of a milk-boy, casting dreadful looks at the brothers while the other boys took him for a friend.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.64: 'adorned with wild flowers', 'assumed the guise of a milk-man... cast his dreadful looks at Krishna and Rohini's son'; BP 10.18.17-18 context.

statements.claim: Krishna knew what he was; the all-seeing Lord welcomed his friendship and resolved his destruction.
statements.evidence: BP 10.18.17 'vidvān api dāśārho bhagavān sarva-darśanaḥ' (though knowing, the Blessed Lord, seer of all); pack excerpt: 'Krishna, who knows all, welcomes his friendship while resolving his destruction.'

statements.claim: Krishna, who knew every game, proposed the riding game of carrying one another on their shoulders and racing.
statements.evidence: BP 10.18.18 'upāhūya gopālān kṛṣṇaḥ prāha vihāra-vit' (calling the cowherds, Krishna, knower of games, spoke); game details follow in 10.18.19-23 (see DKS_0058 pack).

statements.claim: Atmosphere: the stranger appearing at the edge of play, the boys' games and races.
statements.evidence: Generic scene-setting; games of running/leaping/wrestling are standard connective description.

notes: Pralamba's motive and disguise details draw on the Harivamsha passage carried in the adjacent story's pack; consistent with the episode's excerpt.

statements.claim: In the riding game, when Sridama and the other strong boys stood on Balarama's side, even Krishna was defeated and carried Sridama.
statements.evidence: BP 10.18.22-23 'śrīdāma-vṛṣabhādayaḥ... uvāha kṛṣṇo bhagavān śrīdāmānaṃ parājitaḥ' (Krishna, defeated, carried Sridama); the loser-carries-winner rule in Harivamsha 1.64 ('carrying on their shoulders the victorious, those who were vanquished').

statements.claim: Pralamba chose to carry Balarama, having concluded Krishna was beyond his reach and the elder brother the one to take.
statements.evidence: BP 10.18.24 'aviṣahyaṃ manyamānaḥ kṛṣṇaṃ dānava-puṅgavaḥ' (the foremost of demons, deeming Krishna unbearable); Harivamsha 1.64: 'considering Krishna... irrepressible he gave him up and made up his mind for destroying Baladeva.'

statements.claim: Pralamba carried Balarama away, not toward the Bhandira tree but in the opposite direction, and grew into his true demonic form — tall as a tree, clad in gold and ornaments, eyes like chariot wheels, a crown on his head, the earth sinking under his feet.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.64: 'proceeded quickly in an opposite direction', 'huge as the Bhandiraka fig-tree', 'eyes like unto the wheels of a car', 'a head adorned with a sun-like coronet', 'the earth sank under the weight of his feet'; BP 10.18.25-26: 'puraṭa-paricchadaḥ' (clad in gold), blazing with ornaments, bracelets, crown, earrings; carried like a cloud with the moon.

statements.claim: Balarama called out asking Krishna how to overcome the demon, and Krishna answered with a smile that he knew what Balarama truly was and to remember his own strength.
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.64 verses 31-35: 'O Krishna, I am being carried away by this Daitya... How shall I vanquish him?' and Krishna, knowing Rohini's son's strength, smilingly told him to meditate on his own Nārāyaṇa nature.

statements.claim: Balarama struck Pralamba once on the head with a fist like a thunderbolt; the skull shattered, blood ran from his mouth, and he fell dead like a toppled mountain.
statements.evidence: BP 10.18.27-28 'sa āhataḥ sapadi viśīrṇa-mastako mukhād vaman rudhiram' (struck, skull shattered, vomiting blood from the mouth); Harivamsha 1.64: 'with his well-formed fist resembling a thunder-bolt struck the wicked Pralamva on the head'; VP 5.9 and BP 10.18.29 for the fall.

statements.claim: The cowherd boys came running and saw him slain; the brothers returned unhurried.
statements.evidence: BP 10.18.29 'dṛṣṭvā pralambaṃ nihataṃ' (seeing Pralamba slain); the unhurried return is connective.

statements.claim: Atmosphere: the startled moment of the plow-bearer, the laughter of the games.
statements.evidence: BP 10.18.26 'haladhara īṣad atrasat' (the plow-bearer was somewhat startled) supports the startle; rest is framing.

notes: Fist-on-head version follows BP and Harivamsha (VP's knees/eyes variant noted in pack but story uses the primary source).

statements.claim: While the boys played, the cows, goats and buffaloes wandered from one grove to the next, and the boys found the herd gone.
statements.evidence: BP 10.19.1-2 'ajā gāvo mahiṣyaś ca nirviśantyo vanād vanam / te 'paśyantaḥ paśūn gopāḥ' (goats, cows and buffaloes entering forest after forest; the cowherds not seeing the cattle).

statements.claim: They searched by reading the ground: grass cut by hooves and hoof-prints led them on.
statements.evidence: BP 10.19.3 'tṛṇais tat-khura-dac-chinnair goṣ-padair aṅkitair gavām' (marked by grass cut by hooves and hoof-prints of the cows).

statements.claim: The trail led into a dense thicket of munja grass where the herd was found lost and lowing.
statements.evidence: BP 10.19.4 'muñjāṭavyāṃ bhraṣṭa-mārgaṃ krandamānaṃ sva-godhanam' (in the munja forest, the herd off the path, lowing).

statements.claim: Krishna called to the cows with a voice deep as a cloud, and they began to quiet.
statements.evidence: BP 10.19.5 'tā āhūtā bhagavatā megha-gambhīrayā girā' (they were called by the Lord with a voice deep as a cloud); the calming is connective.

statements.claim: A wildfire with smoke for its banner sprang up around them on every side, as if by accident — the destroyer of all that lived in the forest — and the boys and cattle were ringed by flame.
statements.evidence: BP 10.19.6-7 'dava-dhūmaketur yadṛcchayābhūt kṣaya-kṛd vanaukasām... tam āpatantaṃ parito davāgniṃ gopāś ca gāvaḥ... bhītāḥ' (a wildfire with smoke for banner arose by chance, destroyer of forest-dwellers; seeing it approaching all around, cowherds and cows were frightened).

statements.claim: They cried 'Krishna! Krishna! Great hero! O Rama, whose strength never fails!'
statements.evidence: BP 10.19.8 'kṛṣṇa kṛṣṇa mahā-vīra he rāmāmogha vikrama' (Krishna! Krishna! Great hero! O Rama of infallible prowess).

statements.claim: Atmosphere: wind driving the fire forward, tall sharp-bladed munja reeds, the silence of the search.
statements.evidence: Wind and reed-height are generic description; the fire's 'accidental' origin (yadṛcchayā) is supported.

statements.claim: In the rains the forest was the best of forests, heavy with ripening dates and jambu fruit, and Krishna and Balarama led the herd into it.
statements.evidence: BP 10.20.24 'vanaṃ tad varṣiṣṭhaṃ pakva-kharjura-jambumat' (that forest, best in the rains, full of ripe dates and jambu); leading the herd in the pack's index summary.

statements.claim: The cows walked slowly because their udders were heavy with milk.
statements.evidence: BP 10.20.25 'dhenavo manda-gāminya ūdho-bhāreṇa bhūyasā' (cows slow-moving by the great burden of their udders).

statements.claim: The forest-dwellers were delighted, the trees let fall their honey-sweet blossoms, and the boys sheltered under a tree or in a cave when a shower broke.
statements.evidence: BP 10.20.26-27 'vanaukasaḥ pramuditā vana-rājīr madhu-cyutaḥ / kvacid vanaspati-kroḍe guhāyāṃ cābhivarṣati' (forest-dwellers delighted, trees shedding honey; when it rained, in a tree-hollow or cave).

statements.claim: They ate a meal of curd and rice set out on a flat stone near the water, sitting on the green grass, and afterward watched the cows chew their cud with half-closed eyes.
statements.evidence: BP 10.20.28-29 'dadhy-odanaṃ samānītaṃ śilāyāṃ salilāntike / śādvalopari saṃviśya carvato mīlitekṣaṇān' (curd-rice brought, on a stone near the water; seated on the fresh grass, chewing with half-closed eyes).

statements.claim: It was, the verses say, a beauty of the rains that brings happiness in every season.
statements.evidence: BP 10.20.30 'prāvṛṭ-śriyaṃ... sarva-kāla-sukhāvahām' (the glory of the rains, bringing happiness at all times).

statements.claim: No demon, fire or danger came that day; the afternoon passed peacefully.
statements.evidence: Negative framing consistent with the pack — the entire episode 10.20.24-30 is idyllic with no adversary; framing device, no contrary fact asserted.
